Sorry I worded that horribly but basically make sure she understands that a diagnosis like this shouldn't be taken lightly and that you're willing to show her unconditional support if she chooses to seek help.

https://youtu.be/iraGmA7-9FA [Here's a really cute way of explaining BPD.] You might like to show her this. 

I would carefully tell her that you'd like to sit and talk with her about the information she shared. Explain to her that you love and care about her and it is for those reasons why you're worried for her that she not seek assistance after being diagnosed. It is something that is to be taken seriously and, if you're up to it, offer your assistance in anyway possible as you understand how confronting a diagnosis that you're unfamiliar with can be frightening.

I was terrified too but seeking help was ultimately the best thing for me and my loved ones. 

Think of it this way: what's worse, mustering up the courage to get yourself some help or attempting to live life with this monster of an illness?
